thread:
elaine: Hey @ramon @sophia — marketing is finalizing the launch post and webinar deck. We need a compact handoff from eng/runtime so our claims match the artifacts. Can you help with a rerun + validation checklist?

patrick: +1, need numbers for a slide deck and a 2-sentence PR claim. Warmup vs coldstart numbers especially.

elaine: Ideally we want: p50/p90/p99 token-latency, cost per 1k tokens, embed latency (single request), and a coldstart heatmap across 0-5k concurrent requests. Also quantized variant numbers.

ramon: Got it. Quick clarifying q's: which model and sequence length distribution should we use? Also do you need tail percentiles for full-gen or per-token?

elaine: Model = open-llama-70b-quant (the one we plan to cite). Sequence lengths: 16% short (32), 50% medium (256), 34% long (1024). Full-gen percentiles please (end-to-end). We'll also call out a 512-token typical prompt in the PR.

patrick: For the launch claim we say "~2x lower cost vs baseline on 512-token chat" — we need the baseline definition (baseline model & config) so legal is happy.

ramon: Baseline: llama-70b-v1 float32 on 8xA100, no KV caching, batching disabled, cold starts included. We'll run our variant with quantization, prefix caching enabled, and batch size tuned to keep p90 < 200ms target.

sophia: FYI runtime-bot is about to post warmup traces once the run starts. We'll attach raw traces + a minimal reproducible payload pack for your data team.

runtime-bot: starting run 4419876543-quant-embed-tailcase at 2025-11-03T14:12:10Z. Config: model=open-llama-70b-quant, batch_target=0.8, kv_cache=true, warmup_requests=2000

elaine: Thanks. Can you also include the exact CLI and seeds/config so marketing can reproduce the numbers for the press pack? We need: commands, env, random_seed, and a short JSON manifest of sample inputs.

ramon: Will do. Example run command we'll provide:
```
REDWOOD_REGION=us-east-1 
SEED=42 
./run_bench --model open-llama-70b-quant \
  --seq-distribution "32:0.16,256:0.5,1024:0.34" \
  --concurrency-schedule "0-100:10m,100-1k:20m,1k-5k:30m" \
  --batch-target 0.8 \
  --kv-cache on \
  --log-level info \
  --emit-traces /tmp/traces/4419876543
```

sophia: We'll include a small sample artifact pack (10 prompts) plus a larger randomized seed cohort (2k prompts) for QA. Also including quantized and float artifacts.

elaine: Perfect. One more ask: marketing needs a one-paragraph summary that explains methodology in plain English for the blog. Can you draft a sentence like: what we measured, the traffic profile, and how we controlled for variance?

ramon: Draft: "We measured end-to-end generation latency and per-token resource consumption on open-llama-70b across representative prompt lengths. Runs used deterministic seeds and a staged concurrency schedule to capture coldstart behavior and steady-state throughput; KV-prefix caching and quantized execution were enabled on the optimized variant while the baseline used float inference without caching. All results include raw trace artifacts and per-request logs for audit."

patrick: That reads good to me. Can you add a short note about warmup policy so product folks don't misinterpret coldstart curves?

ramon: Add-on line: "Warmup was performed using 2k synthetic requests matching the sequence-length distribution; coldstart points reflect the first 30 seconds after instance boot with no prior cache."

elaine: Excellent. Timeline? We need the artifacts and slide-ready numbers by EOD Friday so design can lock visuals.

ramon: We'll kick off reruns today. ETA for raw artifacts + manifest: 48 hours. ETA for slide-ready summary + single-sheet numbers: 72 hours. If you need faster we can prioritize but results might be noisier.

elaine: 48 hours is okay. Please drop the raw CSVs, heatmap PNG (coldstart vs concurrency), and a single JSON with p50/p90/p99 and cost-per-1k for each variant. Also include embed latency single-request medians.

runtime-bot: run 4419876543-quant-embed-tailcase completed at 2025-11-03T15:03:41Z. Artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/4419876543/{traces.csv,heatmap.png,summary.json,sample-pack.zip}

ramon: Uploading the slide CSVs now. I'll @elaine when public S3 links are ready.

sophia: Also pinging data-eng for an independent spot-check tomorrow morning to validate p99 tail calculation method.

elaine: Thanks everyone — will prep the PR language once we have the summary.json. :rocket:

patrick: Adding note for comms: avoid absolute "2x" wording unless comparison method is shown. We'll frame as "~2x on our test workload; see methodology."

elaine: Good call. We'll use conservative phrasing.

ramon: Links posted: https://s3.redwood.internal/4419876543/summary.json (perm=team), https://s3.redwood.internal/4419876543/heatmap.png

elaine: Got them. Closing loop — will share final PR copy in this thread for a quick sign-off. Thanks!
